## What this is
"Goggins of Gambling" is a mobile-first, **static** betting *analyzer* for Reed and friends (plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no backend). It shows daily picks with neutral reads, a Build a Bet market picker, My Bets (a private bankroll tracker in localStorage), Record (calibration), Fade Trent and Settings. Prices come from Polymarket US (public gateway), Vegas lines from The Odds API, and stats from ESPN's free APIs. **It is an analyzer, not a pick seller.**

## Architecture / file map (detail: HANDOFF §2–§3)
- `index.html` loads every script with a `?v=<version>` cache-buster. `config.js` holds the brand and platforms.
- `js/app.js`: tabs and rendering (Picks, Build a Bet, My Bets, Record, Settings). `js/strings.js` holds **all UI text**.
- `js/picker*.js`: Build a Bet market picker. `js/markets-core.js` normalizes Polymarket US events.
- `js/viz.js`: tap-a-bet pop-up: zoomable live price chart (§48, §53, §55) + prop bet bars.
- `js/our-chance.js`: the **Analytics** blend (§56), shared by the browser and scripts.
- `js/dig-deeper.js`: the Dig deeper sheet + `POSITION_STATS`, the one position-to-stats map (§57).
- `js/evaluate.js` (risk/verdict), `js/calc.js` (payout math), `js/vegas.js` (Vegas lines), `js/plain.js` (plain words), `js/storage.js` (localStorage), `js/positions.js`, `js/teams.js`, `js/gametime.js`, `js/play.js` (play money), `js/trent.js`, `js/share.js`, `js/github-log.js`.
- `css/style.css` (ours) and `css/live-bets.css` (Richie's).
- `data/*.json`: picks, predictions, markets, Vegas lines, history, learning (§5). `scripts/*.mjs` are the jobs that write them.

## Run and test locally
```bash
python3 -m http.server 8765        # open http://localhost:8765/
for f in tests/*.test.mjs tests/*.test.js; do node "$f" || echo "FAIL $f"; done
# headless UI walk-through (optional): npm i --no-save puppeteer-core; CHROME=/usr/bin/google-chrome node tests/smoke.js http://localhost:8765/
```

## Deploy
GitHub Pages serves `main`. **Push to main = deploy** (it's live in about a minute). Before every push that changes the site, run `node scripts/bump-version.mjs`. It stamps `version.json` + every `?v=` in `index.html`, so phones auto-reload (§49). Use descriptive commits and add a HANDOFF § note.

## Data flow and scripts (detail: HANDOFF §8, §13, §17, §36)
- `scripts/update-picks.mjs picks <file>`: validates, runs `scripts/our-chance.mjs` (hit_prob = Analytics), fills risk/verdict, commits. Also `fill`, `grade`, `lineup`, `list`.
- `scripts/fetch-markets.mjs` → `data/markets/`. `scripts/fetch-book-odds.mjs` → `data/vegas-lines.json`, `data/book-odds.json` (needs `ODDS_API_KEY`). `scripts/ingest-vegas.mjs` → `data/vegas-manual.json`.
- `scripts/capture-closing.mjs` → `data/pick-history.json` (logs hit_prob, our_chance, market_chance). `scripts/learn.mjs` → `data/learning.json` (calibration).
- `scripts/archive.mjs` → `data/archive/` (append-only gzip NDJSON for backtests/weight-tuning; schema in `data/archive/README.md`, HANDOFF §59). It runs after capture-closing.
- `scripts/trent-picks.mjs`, `scripts/play-leaderboard.mjs`, `scripts/fetch-positions.mjs`.

## Fade Trent clarifications (dev-only, HANDOFF §58)
Unclear Trent bets are flagged `needs_clarification` + `question` and stay pending.
- **Answer directly:** `node scripts/trent-picks.mjs clarify <id> --set key=value --answer "..." --commit`.
- **Dev vote:** `ask <id> --question ".." --issue --option "A label|k=v" --option "B label|k=v"` opens a `trent-clarify` issue. It @mentions all current collaborators (fetched live; Reed's standing permission, unclear bets only), with one comment per option; devs 👍 to vote. Then run `tally <id> --commit` (tie: reedrice decides).
- **See open questions:** `questions`, or the site with `?dev=1`.

## Token-Efficiency & GitOps Rules

**Sports-data source of truth:** lineups, injuries and goalie availability use the free ESPN flat-file JSON snapshots in `data/espn/`, refreshed by `.github/workflows/live-maintenance.yml` through `scripts/fetch-espn-status.mjs`. Consume those files rather than creating another poller, scraper, ORM, database schema or parallel sports-data store. Improve the existing approved fetcher when necessary; do not create a second ingestion architecture. This storage migration does not imply ESPN supplies every lineup, goalie confirmation or hockey line combination: unavailable evidence remains explicitly unverified.

1. **Native execution is the default requirement.** Build recurring data collection, odds aggregation, parsing, grading, calibration, report text and publication with deterministic JavaScript/Node.js scripts and structured APIs. Store public results as versioned JSON. Do not use an LLM to fetch, copy, summarize or transform data that code can handle.
2. **No new AI monitors.** Do not create agent heartbeats, scheduled ChatGPT/Grok runs, AI retries or model API calls for routine site operations. Development/review agents are on-demand tools, not the production scheduler. The only currently authorized exception is Reed's retained two-hour Fade Trent browser check; it consumes AI usage and must not expand into general sports scraping. Any additional AI exception requires Reed's explicit approval of scope, frequency, cost limits and stop conditions.
3. **Use GitHub Actions for recurring work.** Keep production schedules in .github/workflows/live-maintenance.yml, use the shared production-site concurrency group and owners.json gates, and disable duplicate external/local schedules after handoff. Even an AI wakeup that only checks a gate can consume usage. Sandbox work is explicit manual testing only; never enable copied production schedules there.
4. **Prefer structured sources and honest unknowns.** Use ESPN/exchange JSON APIs, bounded requests, timeouts, caching and deterministic matching. Preserve source URLs, timestamps and failure/coverage states. Never turn missing data, a probable starter or a depth chart into confirmed news. General Underdog/X/Twitter sports scraping is deprecated. Never invoke AI to hide a source failure; use native CI failures/reports and retry on the next permitted run.
5. **Publish through GitOps.** Validate schemas and relevant regression guards, commit only explicitly allowed public files, refresh latest main and regenerate on races, and use fast-forward-only publication. Never overwrite newer openings/history/grades or force-push. Deploy Pages and verify public data after the build delay. No model should be required to keep production running.
6. **Keep credentials and account data private.** Use scoped built-in workflow credentials or approved environment secrets, never literals, logs or committed key files. Private user positions/keys remain on their approved private client origin. Only public sports/record/feedback data enters shared snapshots. Paid data API credits are separate from AI usage; do not silently enable a new paid service.
7. **Guard against regression.** The no-ai-runtime test blocks common model-provider endpoints/SDKs and agent CLI execution in tracked runtime/workflow files. Review all new outbound services and workflow actions; this check is a backstop, not proof against every possible proxy. Document any authorized exception in this file, owners.json and HANDOFF.md.

## Hard rules (non-negotiable)
1. **Privacy:** never commit dollar amounts, bankrolls, stakes, tokens or keys. Money lives only in the user's localStorage.
2. **`ODDS_API_KEY`** is read from the environment only. Never print, log, echo or commit it.
3. **Analyzer, not pick seller:** no bet instructions ("tap No on…"), no suggested bets or stakes, no advice wording on the site. Use neutral reads and examples only ("$10 → $20", the user's own unit). `tests/no-instructions.test.mjs` guards this. How-to-bet help stays in private chat.
4. Say **"prop bets"** (not "props") in UI text.
5. **No cents** anywhere on screen. Show whole dollars and American odds (§29, §52).
6. **Exactly 6 tabs.** New features go in sheets or pop-ups (e.g. Dig deeper), never a new tab.
7. **Analytics** = the blend of history (ESPN, beta-shrunk) + no-vig Vegas + the market, in log-odds, clamped to 3–97% (`js/our-chance.js`). The UI label is "Analytics", never "Our chance".
8. **Position-aware stats:** stat pickers offer only stats that fit the player's ESPN position (`POSITION_STATS` in `js/dig-deeper.js`). Goalies only see goalie stats, skaters never do, and so on.
9. Set user-visible text through `js/strings.js` / textContent. Allow only https links.
10. Follow [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Global UI Design Tokens (Men in Black, Reed Oct 21)

All new or updated layouts must consume css/theme.css, the centralized master theme loaded LAST after style.css and live-bets.css. Plain CSS custom properties are the source of truth; do not add Tailwind/build tooling, a competing theme or component-specific palette/radius overrides. Applies to every main-site screen, navigation bar, secondary workflow, profile, history grid, account setup, settings layer and sheet.

- Universal canvas: --canvas: #0A0E17. Body background is fixed to this value, with no texture/gradient layer.
- Geometry: --radius-panel: 24px for content cards, data panels and sheets; --radius-control: 16px for inputs, buttons, filters and pills. Never invent a third panel/control radius. Circular avatars/team logos and chart data marks retain their semantic geometry.
- Glass elevation for all secondary content containers: --surface-glass: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03); --surface-blur: 12px; --surface-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05). Use background: var(--surface-glass), backdrop-filter: blur(var(--surface-blur)) plus -webkit-backdrop-filter, and border: 1px solid var(--surface-border). No solid local panel fills or bespoke gradients. Native OS option popups use the canvas for legibility.
- Typography: --font-ui is the native Apple/system sans-serif stack; --text-primary: #FFFFFF for headers and choices; --text-secondary: #8E9AA8 for supporting telemetry, dates, odds and labels. Use shared type/weight tokens. Outcome/warning colors and chart/team series remain semantic; do not erase win/loss distinctions.
- Spacing: --module-gap and --panel-padding are 24px; shared spacing scale is 4/8/12/16/24/32px. --page-gutter scales 16–32px. Header, platform nav and bottom tabs use the same glass, colors and control geometry; preserve safe-area padding and six reachable tabs.
- Existing component aliases (--bg, --card, --text, --muted, --radius, --font-head/body) resolve to this master file. Use .mib-panel/.mib-control for future generic surfaces or existing themed component classes. The limited important declarations are migration adapters for legacy ID/inline styling, not a pattern to copy into new components.
- Maintain visible keyboard focus, native input semantics, 44px touch actions, responsive layouts and reduced-motion support. Main-site CSS must never inspect or reach into another user's isolated private account origin. Independently deployed personal panels retain their own deployment boundary.

The backend GitOps/ESPN architecture remains frozen; visual changes must not add AI monitors, data stores, polling loops or alter calculation/settlement meaning.

### User-selectable colorways (Reed follow-up, Oct 21)
The palette is deliberately NOT frozen. Reed rejected the black/orange direction and requested built-in experimentation. Default is Ocean blue; Settings → Appearance also offers Soft violet, Deep teal and Custom canvas/accent pickers. css/theme.css contains the preset overrides; js/theme.js applies validated appearance preferences via Store. Choices persist per device in betdash_prefs, independently of account connections. A custom light canvas uses contrasting dark text/glass tint; custom action text adjusts to accent brightness. This overrides the earlier fixed canvas/text palette requirement for user-selected schemes, while keeping 24px panels, 16px controls, 12px blur and spacing consistent. New UI must consume role tokens so every screen follows the active colorway. No hardcoded orange chrome or separate screen palettes.

Frontend collaborator entry point: read [css/README.md](css/README.md) for the role-token map, theme load order, preset extension steps and appearance verification. These files are committed to main so all collaborators and their agents receive the same rules; no extra automation is required to discover them.

### Card contrast and mobile override (Reed, Oct 21)
Content panels use --surface-panel (7% contrasting glass) and --panel-border (11%); navigation and controls retain the quieter 3%/5% glass. Custom light palettes use black rather than white glass. Existing Live Bets big/slight categories use restrained green/amber tints; score/news-explained moves use the existing warning red, without changing classification or claiming these are new risk grades.
Below 768px, --radius-panel, --panel-padding and --module-gap become 16px. Controls remain 16px. The six-tab dock uses 9px labels and 17px icons with 52px targets and safe-area clearance. The score ticker becomes a manual horizontal flex scroller; duplicate marquee content is hidden. This explicitly supersedes the earlier fixed 24px mobile geometry and identical glass on every surface. Preserve these responsive role tokens in future layouts.
